prompt: Status of the Russian-Ukrainian conflict, as if we are at the end of 2024 heading into 2025.

criteria.name: Shifts in Battlefield Momentum
criteria.description: Assess which side holds the initiative, how frontlines are moving, and whether operations reflect a sustained attritional push or periods of stalemate and localized breakthroughs.

criteria.name: Force Generation Capacity
criteria.description: Evaluate both sides’ ability to recruit, mobilize, and retain personnel, including indicators of recruitment incentives, coercive measures, and strain on available manpower.

criteria.name: Equipment and Industrial Sustainment
criteria.description: Examine the replenishment of armored vehicles, artillery, drones, and missiles through domestic production, refurbishment of older stocks, and external sourcing, and whether loss rates outpace resupply.

criteria.name: Airpower and Air Defense Balance
criteria.description: Analyze the evolving advantage in the air, including the effectiveness of air defenses, the intensity of drone and missile campaigns, and the impact of stand-off munitions on frontline and urban targets.

criteria.name: Energy Infrastructure Targeting
criteria.description: Track patterns of strikes on power generation and distribution, their impact on civilian resilience and industrial output, and how seasons or resource constraints influence targeting strategies.

criteria.name: Cross-Border Strike Dynamics
criteria.description: Assess the scope and frequency of long-range strikes beyond the frontline, the types of targets selected, and how policy constraints or authorizations affect escalation and deterrence.

criteria.name: External Aid and Policy Shifts
criteria.description: Monitor changes in foreign military and financial assistance, legal or political restrictions on weapons use, and how allied rearmament priorities affect support timelines and volumes.

criteria.name: Negotiation Prospects and Preconditions
criteria.description: Identify signals regarding potential talks, including maximalist demands, ceasefire preconditions, and whether battlefield pressure is used to shape bargaining positions.

criteria.name: Domestic Political Will and Morale
criteria.description: Evaluate societal tolerance for casualties and economic costs, elite cohesion, propaganda narratives, and how battlefield outcomes influence public support on each side and among allies.

criteria.name: Regional Spillover and Buffer Tactics
criteria.description: Analyze attempts to create buffer zones or cross-border incursions aimed at reducing enemy strike capacity, and the consequent redistribution of forces along the front.

criteria.name: Winter Warfare and Seasonality Effects
criteria.description: Assess how weather and terrain conditions alter operational tempo, logistics, and targeting priorities, especially regarding energy systems and urban centers.

criteria.name: Sanctions and War Economy Adaptation
criteria.description: Examine how sanctions, shadow supply chains, and commodity revenues shape each side’s ability to finance and equip the war effort over time.

criteria.name: Humanitarian Impact and Displacement
criteria.description: Track trends in civilian exposure to violence, infrastructure disruption, displacement flows, and the adequacy of mitigation measures and social services.

criteria.name: Defense-in-Depth and Fortification Quality
criteria.description: Assess the robustness of defensive lines, the transition to new positions after losses, and vulnerability to stand-off bombardment and combined-arms assaults.

criteria.name: Escalation Risks and Nuclear Signaling
criteria.description: Monitor rhetoric and posture related to strategic weapons, thresholds that could trigger broader escalation, and how such signaling influences allied policy.

criteria.name: Drone and Counter-Drone Innovation
criteria.description: Evaluate the pace of unmanned systems development, electronic warfare adaptations, and shifting cost-exchange ratios in the air and on the front.

criteria.name: Logistics and Sustainment Lines
criteria.description: Analyze the security of supply routes and hubs, interdiction efforts, and how strikes on transportation and depots affect operational reach.

criteria.name: Allied Cohesion and Burden-Sharing
criteria.description: Assess unity among supporting states, divergence in threat perceptions, and the balance between assisting the conflict and rearming domestically.

criteria.name: Prospects for Breakthrough vs. Attrition
criteria.description: Judge whether either side can mass sufficient capability for a decisive breach, or if trends point to continued grinding attrition with incremental territorial changes.

criteria.name: Civil Defense and Resilience Measures
criteria.description: Examine adaptation to sustained strikes—air raid protection, grid hardening, dispersal of industry—and their effectiveness in reducing damage and maintaining functionality.

criterion_scores.name: Shifts in Battlefield Momentum
criterion_scores.explanation: Clearly characterizes late-2024 tempo: intensified Donbas battles, Q4 surges, localized spikes, and lack of decisive breakthrough pointing to attritional equilibrium. Mentions Kursk incursion and episodic Black Sea pulses. Minor gap: limited explicit discussion of which side holds overall initiative beyond suggesting stalemate.

criterion_scores.name: Force Generation Capacity
criterion_scores.explanation: Only brief, high-level references to manpower pressures and recruitment/retention are absent. No detail on mobilization waves, incentives, exemptions, coercive measures, rotation, or casualty replacement on either side.

criterion_scores.name: Equipment and Industrial Sustainment
criterion_scores.explanation: Notes Western production shortfalls for air defense, shells, counter‑drone kits and Russia tapping external suppliers; mentions resource constraints. Lacks specifics on domestic production rates, refurbishment of legacy armor/artillery, or quantitative loss vs resupply comparisons.

criterion_scores.name: Airpower and Air Defense Balance
criterion_scores.explanation: Touches on long-range precision strikes, stand-off munitions, drone and missile activity, Black Sea pulses, and increased lethality patterns. However, limited analysis of air-defense effectiveness, sortie rates, SEAD/DEAD efforts, and comparative air advantage.

criterion_scores.name: Energy Infrastructure Targeting
criterion_scores.explanation: Mentions renewed strikes on critical infrastructure and increased civilian-targeting incidents but provides little detail on power generation/distribution impacts, seasonality of energy strikes, or grid performance metrics.

criterion_scores.name: Cross-Border Strike Dynamics
criterion_scores.explanation: Strong coverage: detailed trends in Belgorod/Kursk/Bryansk, H2 lethality surge, event-to-fatality distributions, high-volume-low-lethality Belgorod vs lethal spikes in Kursk, routine remote violence characterization.

criterion_scores.name: External Aid and Policy Shifts
criterion_scores.explanation: Addresses NATO/EU support continuity, Russia’s backing from China/Iran/North Korea, sanctions/export controls and administrative drag. Missing are concrete aid volumes, timing lags, legal constraints on weapons use, or notable 2024 policy inflections by key donors.

criterion_scores.name: Negotiation Prospects and Preconditions
criterion_scores.explanation: Argues toward negotiated stalemate in 2025 due to polarization and attrition. Does not enumerate explicit preconditions, maximalist demands, or concrete diplomatic signals, though it ties battlefield pressure to bargaining space.

criterion_scores.name: Domestic Political Will and Morale
criterion_scores.explanation: Hints at societal strain, displacement, and alliance polarization but lacks discussion of public opinion trends, elite cohesion, propaganda narratives, protests, or morale indicators in Russia, Ukraine, and allied states.

criterion_scores.name: Regional Spillover and Buffer Tactics
criterion_scores.explanation: Covers cross-border strikes and mentions incursion into Kursk, implying attempts to shape enemy capacity. Limited exploration of declared buffer-zone concepts, redistribution of forces along the front, or sustained cross-border ground holds.

criterion_scores.name: Winter Warfare and Seasonality Effects
criterion_scores.explanation: Notes escalation into winter, Q4 battle surges, and suggests energy and logistics pressures, but offers little detail on mud/freeze impacts, mobility, maintenance, or seasonal targeting strategies besides generalities.

criterion_scores.name: Sanctions and War Economy Adaptation
criterion_scores.explanation: Mentions tightened sanctions, shadow supply via external backers, and administrative burdens; acknowledges both sides’ resource constraints. Lacks depth on evasion networks, revenue streams, budgetary measures, or industrial adaptation specifics.

criterion_scores.name: Humanitarian Impact and Displacement
criterion_scores.explanation: Addresses persistent mass displacement, host-country integration challenges, strain on municipal services, and rising civilian-targeting incidents with scale figures. Could expand on internal displacement flows and service provision metrics.

criterion_scores.name: Defense-in-Depth and Fortification Quality
criterion_scores.explanation: Infers attritional fights and localized lethality patterns but does not analyze trench systems, minefields, layered defenses, fallback lines, or vulnerability to stand-off/combined-arms tactics.

criterion_scores.name: Escalation Risks and Nuclear Signaling
criterion_scores.explanation: Discusses alliance polarization and cross-border strikes but provides no analysis of nuclear rhetoric, thresholds, or strategic posture changes influencing allied policy.

criterion_scores.name: Drone and Counter-Drone Innovation
criterion_scores.explanation: Core theme: drones drive up to 75% of losses, sensor-to-shooter fusion, AI-enabled targeting, cost/tempo effects, and battlefield adaptation. Some mention of counter‑drone needs, though specifics on EW/countermeasures could be deeper.

criterion_scores.name: Logistics and Sustainment Lines
criterion_scores.explanation: Touches on supply chain resilience for munitions/air-defense and resource constraints but lacks detailed analysis of interdiction of rail/road hubs, depots, bridging, and how logistics affect operational reach.

criterion_scores.name: Allied Cohesion and Burden-Sharing
criterion_scores.explanation: Highlights polarization, administrative drag in aid, and competing rearmament priorities broadly. Missing is granular discussion of divergences within NATO/EU, domestic politics affecting aid, and concrete burden-sharing data.

criterion_scores.name: Prospects for Breakthrough vs. Attrition
criterion_scores.explanation: Consistently argues for intensifying but indecisive attrition with incremental gains; explains why support levels avert collapse but don’t enable decisive breach. Strong linkage to 2025 outlook.

criterion_scores.name: Civil Defense and Resilience Measures
criterion_scores.explanation: Notes increased civilian-targeting incidents and strains on emergency services; references the need for protection measures and grid strikes. Limited detail on shelters, air-raid systems, grid hardening, dispersal of industry, or measured effectiveness.
